summary: Design harmonised indicators, data governance, and donor reporting workflows for regional programmes. Build your practical MEAL systems blueprint.
lede: MEAL systems design connects shared results and indicators with practical data workflows, governance and reporting. It is for experienced MEAL practitioners and programme managers who need to coordinate evidence across distributed programme teams, and covers adapting indicators to programme contexts, tracing data flows and strengthening data quality. Participants develop governance and accountability approaches, dashboard specifications and donor-reporting crosswalks, while considering consent, sensitive-data handling and learning use.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for evidence, accountability, data architecture, programme performance, and donor reporting across regional or multi-country initiatives. It suits intermediate and advanced practitioners who already work with programme results and need to coordinate systems across country boundaries.
prerequisites: You should have working experience with monitoring, evaluation, accountability, learning, programme results frameworks, or donor-funded reporting. Familiarity with spreadsheets and at least one digital data collection or reporting platform will help, but no coding or programming experience is required. Advanced interoperability, federated analytics, and AI-assisted quality checks are taught at operational application and conceptual awareness levels, not production-engineering level. Bring a representative indicator list, reporting template, or data-flow example if organizational confidentiality permits.
